Triggered by: inspection INS-0045-0001 on 2022-10-20 Report written: 16 Nov 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0045-0001 showed the wellhead at 24.8 °C with the air at 22.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0045-018

Asset: WELL-0045 (SW-23 Well 045, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 29 Jan 2025 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 73 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0045-0115 on 2025-01-23 Report written: 30 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0045-0115 showed the wellhead at 13.7 °C with the air at 10.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.
